label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7), spilling into the first 1-2 copy steps
explanation: Fires mainly at the delimiter step: 74% of activation mass is at <DEL>, where it is active in 42% of all sequences. The firing rate climbs steeply with sequence length: at <DEL> it is active about 77% of the time when L>=7 and about 89% when L>=8, and rarely when L<=5. The rest of the mass is on the first copy steps (recall_idx 1: 18%, recall_idx 2: 6%). These are more likely when the first original token, which is output at <DEL>, is one of v/m/u/w/b/t. Every top-activating example is <DEL> in an L=8-9 sequence, usually followed by weaker firing on the next copy step or two. It almost never fires in the original phase (1.5% of mass, only near the end of L=9 sequences) or late in the copy phase. The predicate misses the copy-step spillover (recall 0.59, mass recall 0.71), and it has false positives at <DEL> in long sequences whose first token is k/q/f/d/a/c. Adding a first-token clause for recall_idx 1 only improved F1 from 0.67 to 0.69.
